title: GM brings Gemini to 4 million vehicles with Google built in

 GM brings Gemini to 4 million vehicles with Google built in
 Published on November 16, 2026 | Translated from Spanish 
 Category: Technology and AI › Artificial intelligence 
 General Motors announced on April 28, 2026, that Gemini will soon arrive in 2022 and newer Cadillac, Chevrolet, Buick, and GMC vehicles with built-in Google in the United States. We are talking about some 4 million eligible vehicles. The rollout starts only in the U.S. and in English, and GM is already preparing its own AI with OnStar data for later on.
 From Google Assistant to Gemini: the technical leap in infotainment 🚗
 The change involves replacing the current assistant with a language model integrated into the Android Automotive-based infotainment system. Gemini will handle natural language queries, vehicle function control, and contextual responses. Compatibility covers models from 2022 onward, which requires software adjustments on hardware already in circulation. Volvo had already announced a similar move in June 2025 for its cars with built-in Google, marking a trend among manufacturers betting on conversational AI on board.
 Your car now comments on traffic with more style 🗣️
 What was missing was for the car not only to warn you about the traffic jam, but to comment on it fluently while suggesting an alternative route and, along the way, recommending a podcast. With Gemini on board, the conversation with the vehicle goes up a level: it will no longer be a robot that repeats instructions, but a chatty copilot that perhaps knows too much. It remains to be seen whether the driver appreciates so much conversation or ends up asking their own dashboard for silence.
